text:
Jon: quick puzzler  retrofit+okhttp sample app shows body already consumed when retrying auth on Android 13 device. Happens only after enabling streaming uploads in sample.

Maya: can you paste stack + client config?

Jon: stack: 
```
java.io.IOException: Request body already consumed
 at okhttp3.internal.http2.Http2ExchangeCodec.writeRequestBody(Http2ExchangeCodec.java:...)
```
client: ```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .build()
```

Carlos: likely because the interceptor replays the request after refresh but the request body is a non-repeatable streaming body. Retrofit's @Body stream isn't rewindable by default. On newer devices timing exposes this.

Maya: short fixes: 1) mark uploads as repeatable by buffering small bodies (okio.buffer()) or using Multipart which can be retried; 2) for large streams, avoid automatic auth retry and surface a 401 to caller so they can re-upload with a fresh token; 3) document this in the sample app and SDK migration notes.

Jon: implemented buffering for small test fixtures, and added a check in AuthInterceptor to skip automatic retry when request.body is streaming (Content-Length unset). Tests pass locally.

android-ci: Build 4012 passed (emulator API 33) - added unit to detect non-repeatable bodies and log a warning.

Carlos: nice. follow-ups: add a small note to the onboarding README about streaming uploads and auth retries, and consider exposing a helper `OkHttpClientFactory.safeForUploads()` in the SDK.

Jon: will open PR and RFC. thanks!
